newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican Republic cracks down on migration racket.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Republic cracks down on migration racket.

text.p: The United States and Canada are helping Dominican Republic authorities crack down on a network of forgers supplying false documents to illegal immigrants to the United States, a Dominican official said on Thursday.

Deputy Director General of Immigration Manuel Crespo said the network had sent hundreds of Chinese, Cubans and other nationals to Puerto Rico and elsewhere in the United States. Under an accord with Washington, the Dominican Republic will receive special equipment to detect false documents, he said.
Canada is helping to train personnel.
Crespo said Dominicans and foreigners were involved in the network and officials of the former government of President Joaquin Balaguer had taken bribes to cooperate with it.
"They counted on the support of these officials, who for a large sum of money could easily arrange for them to get passports and travel to the United States," Crespo said.

A group of 39 Chinese who tried to get to the United States illegally has been held by immigration authorities for nearly a year. They have not been repatriated because neither China nor Taiwan acknowledges them as citizens.
Crespo said they were victims of the network.

U.S. Coast Guard officials say illegal emigration from the Dominican Republic has increased dramatically in the past year, with smugglers running boatloads of Dominicans and other nationals across the sea to Puerto Rico, a U.S. commonwealth, from where it is easy to reach the U.S. mainland.
